scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: URGENT!! The Internet Lab has DISAPPEARED for the whole
Office department!! All morning none of the 128.168.0.x machines answer any of
our PCs, the 192.168.3.x ones -- everything else works, it's just the lab
that's gone. Something around the link that carries us over to the Internet
Lab must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at the connection
and get us back to their machines? We need them TODAY!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I cannot reproduce the reported outage. Connectivity between the Office LAN (192.168.3.0/24) and the Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16) is healthy end-to-end right now. From multiple Office hosts (office_pc, enquiry, exam_cell, tpo) I successfully pinged several Internet Lab PCs (pc2 128.168.0.2, pc3 .3, pc4 .4, pc5 .5) with 0% packet loss and low RTTs (e.g., office_pc→pc3: 4/4 received; enquiry/exam_cell/tpo→pc2/pc3/pc4/pc5: all 3/3). Reverse direction also works (pc2→office_pc: 3/3). 

Routing across the inter-router link is correct. On router1 (Office side), FRR shows a RIP-learned route “R>* 128.168.0.0/16 via 20.20.0.2, eth3,” and directly connected 192.168.3.0/24 on eth0. On router2 (Internet Lab side), 128.168.0.0/16 is directly connected on eth1, and 192.168.3.0/24 is RIP-learned via 20.20.0.1. Interfaces on the interconnect (router1 eth3 20.20.0.1 and router2 eth2 20.20.0.2) are up and passing traffic.

Affected component: none observed; the inter-site routing and link are functioning. Mechanism: successful ICMP and valid routing tables indicate bidirectional reachability. Localization: N/A (no fault found). Root cause: Not reproducible; likely a transient condition or a host-side issue earlier in the morning. Corrective fix: None required now. If the issue recurs, capture timestamps and MAC/IP of affected PCs, verify their default gateway (192.168.3.1), and collect ARP tables on router1/Office PCs to spot stale entries; consider enabling basic link/RIP monitoring to catch transient events.
